events.html: I give presentations to schools, libraries, museums, and community organizations, both in person and virtually. My talks explore the stories behind my books and the storytelling power of comics and I do my best to adapt each presentation to the audience. Programs include a behind-the-scenes look at my creative process and conclude with a Q&A with the audience.

events.label: This Award winning graphic novel is based on the true story of a Jewish immigrant who helped hi
events.html: This Award winning graphic novel is based on the true story of a Jewish immigrant who helped his Japanese-American neighbors when they were incarcerated during WWII. Through a visually engaging presentation, Tuininga shares the intricacies of his research and creative process, unraveling the profound lessons embedded in these tales of allyship and unity amidst the turbulence of wartime.

events.label: Sequential: The Storytelling Power of Comic Books
events.html: Sequential: The Storytelling Power of Comic Books

events.label: Despite the graphic novel’s skyrocketing popularity, many still see comics as less serious than
events.html: Despite the graphic novel’s skyrocketing popularity, many still see comics as less serious than traditional literature. In this talk, comic artist Josh Tuininga challenges that assumption, revealing how graphic novels engage readers in uniquely powerful ways. Tracing the surprising history of sequential art, Tuininga shows how comics have shaped culture, challenged conventions, and opened new possibilities for storytelling for artists and readers of all ages.

A GRAFFITI STORY

COMING 2/16/27
Graphic Memoir (Abrams ComicArts 2023)

An autobiographical YA graphic novel set in Seattle in the early 1990s. After a life-threatening neurological diagnosis and brain surgery leave him struggling to find his place, Josh discovers solace and purpose in Seattle’s vibrant underground graffiti scene. When he and a friend stumble upon a flyer for a legendary graffiti competition, they set out to make a name for themselves—risking arrest, family trust, and their futures in pursuit of artistic recognition. Fueled by creativity, friendship, and a diverse community of mentors and fellow artists, this true coming-of-age story offers a fresh, nuanced look at the often misunderstood world of graffiti while exploring resilience, identity, and the healing power of art.

index.html:
INSPIRED BY A TRUE STORY
(Abrams ComicArts 2023)

When Marco Calvo arrives at the Jewish Synagogue to attend his grandfather's funeral, he is caught off guard by something very unexpected. Among his close family and friends there are some people he doesn't recognize at all. Several Japanese American families have arrived and no one is quite sure why they are here. Who are these strangers that knew his grandfather so well?
